content.user_title: Stress-Test Decisions With a Review Panel
content.value_statement: Important decisions can retain hidden assumptions when reviewed by one perspective. This skill assigns independent review lenses and combines concrete findings before you finalize a plan.
actual_capabilities: Selects three to five distinct review lenses for an in-session decision.
Guides parallel fork agents to produce read-only, adversarial review reports.
Requires specific corrections, evidence, and severity labels instead of general praise.
Combines duplicate findings while preserving the strength of agreement.
Explains conflicts between review lenses and prioritizes proposed changes.
Routes code diffs and single external checks to more suitable tools.
limitations: It requires the design, plan, or decision to already exist in the current session.
It provides review guidance and does not modify code or files.
Fork agents can share model biases and are not fully independent external reviewers.
It does not replace domain experts, formal testing, or security audits.

use_cases.title: Finalize an architecture decision
use_cases.description: Challenge constraints, failure modes, implementation details, and operational ownership before approving an architecture.

use_cases.title: Review a product policy
use_cases.description: Compare policy consistency, edge cases, enforcement feasibility, and opportunity cost before publication.

use_cases.title: Improve a delivery plan
use_cases.description: Find missing dependencies, risky assumptions, and unclear success measures in an implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Quick decision check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a light Braintrust review of the decision we just discussed. Use three independent lenses and list only concrete changes.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture challenge
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current architecture proposal with lenses for consistency, failure modes, implementation feasibility, and operations. Reconcile the findings.

prompt_templates.title: Policy red team
prompt_templates.prompt: Red-team the policy in this session. Use five orthogonal lenses, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and prioritize fixes by severity and agreement.

prompt_templates.title: Decision with external validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a thorough Braintrust review of this irreversible decision. After synthesis, identify questions that need one independent advisor review.

output_examples.input: Review a database migration plan before approval.
output: High: Add a tested rollback path for partially completed migrations.
Medium: Define ownership for post-migration monitoring.
Decision: Approve after rollback testing and monitoring ownership are documented.
Conflict: Fast escalation may reduce evidence preservation.
Recommended change: Define a severity threshold that requires evidence capture before escalation.
Open question: Confirm the threshold with the on-call team.

best_practices: Place the complete decision context in the current session before starting the panel.
Choose review lenses that examine different failure modes.
Treat panel output as evidence for a decision, not as an automatic decision.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a replacement for a code diff review.
Do not ask every reviewer to use the same broad lens.
Do not force reviewers to invent problems when evidence is absent.

faq.question: What does Braintrust review?
faq.answer: It reviews important in-session designs, plans, policies, and decisions.

faq.question: How many reviewers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses three to five fork agents with different review lenses.

faq.question: Does it edit files?
faq.answer: No. The review process is read-only and produces findings and recommendations.

faq.question: Should I use it for code changes?
faq.answer: Use a dedicated code diff review tool for code changes.

faq.question: Can it replace external validation?
faq.answer: No. Important decisions may still need domain experts or an independent advisor.

faq.question: Why use different lenses?
faq.answer: Different lenses reduce repeated feedback and reveal more types of failure.
